question: The selling price of 35 books is equal to the cost price of 28 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** of 35 books to **Cost Price (CP)** of 28 books is given as equal.

35 × SP = 28 × CP ⇒ SP ÷ CP = 28 ÷ 35 = 4 ÷ 5.

Since SP [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Selling Price of 35 books = Cost Price of 28 books.

**Formulas:** Loss = CP − SP | Loss% = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d83a88734990267fd21564ddcc61407287085d427e832f4722199d134d528a1.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 book be 1 unit.

⇒ CP of 28 books = 28 units and CP of 35 books = 35 units.

⇒ According to the question, **Selling Price (SP)** of 35 books = 28 units.

⇒ Loss = CP of 35 books − SP of 35 books = 35 − 28 = 7 units.

⇒ Loss% = (7 ÷ 35) × 100 = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%.

**∴ The correct answer is 20% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss and Gain Basic Concepts

When SP > CP, it is a **Gain**. Gain% = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100. When CP > SP, it is a **Loss**.

Inverse Relation of Articles

If CP of 'x' articles = SP of 'y' articles, Profit/Loss% = ((x − y) ÷ y) × 100. Positive result means Profit, negative means Loss.</p
